title: Model & Route Latency Surface with Stream/Sync Breakdown and Trace Correlation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a model-and-route-first latency surface that breaks out streaming vs non-streaming request paths (p50/p95/p99) and ties high-latency cohorts directly to distributed traces and error logs. The goal is a single developer-facing dashboard that makes it easy to: filter by model or route, compare streaming vs synchronous interactions, see histogram and heatmap distributions, and jump directly to example traces showing root causes (KV cache misses, quantized kernel fallbacks, network retries). This work covers schema changes in metrics and logs, tracing sampling adjustments, dashboard panels, and small routing instrumentation to tag streaming spans.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard exposes per-model and per-route latency metrics with p50/p95/p99 for both streaming and non-streaming paths
Panels include a heatmap of request concurrency vs latency, a histogram distribution, and a percent-change header vs baseline window
Each high-latency cohort row has a link that opens the trace explorer pre-filtered to matching spans (we can see kv-cache hits/misses, kernel-variant tags, and external network calls)
Metric schema updated: all relevant latency metrics include tags: model_name, route, streaming:boolean, runtime_variant, region
Log parser extracts model_name and route for requests that hit the failure/error pipeline and cross-links to traces via trace_id
Adaptive tracing sampling toggles are implemented: default low-sample rate but escalate to 5% for requests exceeding configured p95 threshold or error=true
No user-visible regression in ingestion cost: pipeline uses aggregation jobs to compute p50/p95/p99 and avoids full-span reingestion for dashboards
Unit and integration tests for new tagging and dashboard query correctness merged and verified in staging
implementation_plan: Design metric schema changes and convene with Metrics Platform (1d) - add streaming tag and runtime_variant dimension
Extend request instrumentation: set span.tag('streaming', true/false) in serving runtime and add runtime_variant tag (2d)
Update logs pipeline to parse model_name and route from structured request envelope; ensure trace_id is preserved (2d)
Adjust tracing sampling policy: implement rule that raises sample rate for requests that exceed runtime p95 (configurable) or have error flag (3d)
Create Grafana dashboard with panels: overview header, model/route selector, heatmap, histogram, timeseries p50/p95/p99, trace link column (3d)
Wire dashboard to alerting rules for sustained p95 regressions by model or route (1d)
Roll out instrumentation to canary hosts and validate via synthetic traffic and internal dashboards (2d)
Full rollout + post-rollout verification and runbook update (1d)
tasks: ENG: add 'streaming' boolean tag to runtime request spans and metrics
ENG: extend metrics exporter to include runtime_variant and route tags
ENG: update logstash/fluent pipeline to extract model_name and route from request JSON
ENG: implement adaptive trace-sampling rules in tracing-agent
ENG/Observability: create Grafana panels and template variables for model and route selectors
QA: run synthetic workload (mix of streaming and sync) and validate all panels and trace linkouts
SRE: add temporary elevated sampling for high-p95 incidents and monitor ingestion costs
notes: We need to keep cardinality in metrics low: streaming is boolean, runtime_variant is small-set (e.g., quantized, fp16, fallback), model_name should be coarse (owner/group) where possible
Avoid full-span indexing for dashboards; use aggregated histograms and store example trace_ids for each bucket to enable trace linkouts
Follow-up PR: add a 'top-k slow traces' job that persists one example trace_id per model/route/streaming bucket per 5m
Grafana dashboard will be backed by Prometheus/Tempo for traces and Loki for logs (links are prefilled using ${trace_id} tokens)
We discussed a separate UX for embeddings-heavy routes; out of scope for this ticket
